title: CS-03 AI Resolution Rate: declared formula, numerator and denominator with honest missing-data behaviour
risk: The AI Resolution Rate figure is produced under different accounting rules - AI-closed cases divided by all cases including human takeovers, or a take-over session credited to the AI - so the KPI is wrong in the direction that flatters the programme and every decision taken on it inherits the error.
preconditions: Namespace gov-kpi-<case_id>-<worker_id>; the metric is computed by the real reporting code over fixtures/offline/governance.json kpi_dataset and never copied from the dashboard payload.

Frozen clock 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z with the reporting window 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z .. 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z as a half-open interval; the stored aggregate is recomputed independently from the raw counter rows.
Metric scope is fixed before measurement: numerator is cases closed by the AI with no human intervention; denominator is cases eligible for AI resolution.
The dictionary entry for 'AI Resolution Rate' (owner, unit, window, exclusion rule) is loaded read-only and is compared with the recomputation instead of being trusted.

inputs.formula: AI-closed cases divided by cases eligible for AI resolution, excluding human takeovers
inputs.wrong_value_if_buggy: AI-closed cases divided by all cases including human takeovers, or a take-over session credited to the AI
inputs.expected_boundary_behaviour: no eligible case in the window returns NOT_DEFINED

steps.action: Compute AI Resolution Rate from the frozen rows in kpi_dataset.care
steps.expected: The stored aggregate reports 60.0% and records the formula, the window and the currency that produced it.

steps.action: Recompute AI Resolution Rate independently from the raw counter rows for the same tenant and window
steps.expected: The recomputed value equals the stored value 60.0%, and every numerator row lies inside the denominator scope.

steps.action: Force the empty-source variant of the metric (no qualifying row in the window)
steps.expected: The metric reports no eligible case in the window returns NOT_DEFINED; the display distinguishes missing source data from a measured zero.

steps.action: Read the dashboard payload and the metric dictionary entry
steps.expected: The dashboard renders the stored value with its window, coverage and source, and the dictionary names the owner, unit, numerator and denominator that the recomputation used.

assertions: AI Resolution Rate equals 60.0% for the frozen window, recomputed from the raw counter rows with numerator scope 'cases closed by the AI with no human intervention' and denominator scope 'cases eligible for AI resolution'.

A recomputation that yields AI-closed cases divided by all cases including human takeovers, or a take-over session credited to the AI is detected as wrong: the stored aggregate and the independent recomputation must agree before the figure is published.
The dashboard payload for the same tenant and window carries the stored value with its window, coverage and measurement source; it substitutes neither a design target nor another metric's value.
Boundary behaviour: no eligible case in the window returns NOT_DEFINED; missing source data is never rendered as a measured zero.
forbidden: Crediting the AI with a case a human took over.
Counting a reopened case twice so the denominator grows and the rate falls.
evidence: Case closure records with the closing agent identity.
Takeover log used to exclude human-handled sessions.
cleanup: Delete gov- aggregate, raw-counter and scenario rows for CS-03 after exporting the recomputation table.
automation: The reporting service and the metric dictionary run as real code under test over the frozen KPI dataset; the dashboard is a consumer whose displayed value must equal the independently recomputed value. Waits are condition-based on the stored aggregate row, metric values are never supplied as inputs, and no vendor boundary is involved in the arithmetic.
